summary: System shows strong architectural patterns for the modernization platform but critical security vulnerabilities in legacy VB6 code that must be addressed during modernization. High risk of data breach and compliance violations if legacy patterns are preserved.

hotspots.reason: SQL injection vulnerabilities in all database operations using string concatenation

provenance.evidence: SELECT Balance FROM tblCustomers WHERE AccountNo=" & txtAccountNo.Text
UPDATE tblCustomers SET Balance = Balance + " & txtAmount.Text

hotspots.reason: No validation, error handling, or audit trails for financial operations

provenance.evidence: Direct balance updates without validation or logging

hotspots.reason: No connection pooling, transaction management, or error recovery

provenance.evidence: Direct ADO recordset operations without proper resource management

risks.title: Critical SQL Injection Vulnerability
risks.description: Legacy VB6 code constructs SQL queries through string concatenation, allowing attackers to manipulate database operations and potentially access or modify unauthorized data

risks.title: No Financial Transaction Validation
risks.description: Banking operations lack input validation, business rule enforcement, and audit trails required for financial systems

risks.title: Missing Authentication and Authorization
risks.description: No evidence of user authentication or authorization checks for sensitive banking operations

risks.title: Compliance Risk
risks.description: Current implementation likely violates PCI DSS, SOX, and other financial regulations due to security gaps
